description.text: Lowland market town near the foot of the mountains. Korvash's clan fled here; his aunt Veshra raised him here.
Tin-masked hobgoblin captain of the Iron Tallies warband; notches a rod for every raid. Overran Korvash's village.
Day 2: his hobgoblins captured Korvash at Cinder Ford. Korvash's greataxe (with Dargan's sash), handaxes and javelins were taken and are kept in the camp's baggage pile near the captain's tent.

Day 2 dawn: speaks Common, calm and dry. Offers Korvash a bargain: swear on his word to serve the Iron Tallies as a hired axe for one year and one day, and the children go free to Harrowmere. Knows Dargan's name and recognized the ember-red sash. Wears a tin mask; has both hands (Dargan did not take his hand; Dargan lost his own).

Refused to free the children before Korvash swears; counter-offer: Korvash swears now, then walks with the line under escort to Harrowmere's border, where the children are cut loose. Korvash's cord is secretly parted behind his back (Day 2, 5:18 AM).
Day 2: accepted Korvash's oath. Wants him at the head of the line. Axe returns at the border stones. Has told Korvash to rest first; camp breaks around noon.
Two moons before Day 2 he ordered his patrol NOT to hunt the small cloaked figure seen at Dargan's cairn. Reason unknown.

Day 2 noon: Asked why he spared the figure at the cairn, he said: 'Some marks on my rod are not for notching. You'll have the answer at the stones, with your axe in your hand.' Deferred. Marches the line south toward Harrowmere's border stones; first night's halt at an abandoned drovers' fold.

Day 2 night, in his tent: told Korvash (truthfully) that at the Goat's Throat he offered Dargan the children's lives for the axe, and Dargan refused. After the raid one child of the clan was never accounted for on his count; he notched the rod for her, then struck it out. He does not know whether the hooded figure is Tessa. He has never hunted it and wants it found by no one else. Insight natural 20: he is afraid of the Greyshaft Foreman, owes him a quota, and freeing the children short-counts him; Korvash's oath was meant to cover the shortfall. He will keep his word to free the children anyway.

Day 11 ~1 AM at the cairn: says he arrived just after the fresh cuts were made; the figure was gone. Admits he saw a small figure slip through the goat-path while Dargan held the Throat and let her go, a debt to Dargan, and has watched for her since to keep the Foreman's scouts from finding her. Greyshaft wants a dragonborn axe-and-fire for the smelter galleries; Korvash is to report to Greyshaft's gate by midwinter's eve. Gorrak offers: leave at dawn, three days' road.

Day 19 ~1:10 PM: met Korvash's column on the high road beyond the stream with about twenty Iron Tally hobgoblins; halted his column and came forward with Sergeant Ushk, rod in hand. Foreman's scouts shadow the column from the ridges.

Day 19 ~1:20 PM: Korvash met him alone on the road and pleaded for the children's passage (Persuasion 6, failed). Gorrak did not refuse outright but said he cannot let ninety-four short-counted hands walk past with the Foreman's riders watching; he demands Korvash's year-and-a-day oath be honored now, in exchange for a delay. Ushk uneasy. Terms are not yet settled.

Day 19 ~1:25 PM: Korvash stepped up and told him privately that the girl he let go over the ledge is in the ditch, then publicly offered himself, his axe and his year-and-a-day to be taken to Greyshaft if the children go free. Gorrak was shaken by the mention of Tessa, accepted the trade in principle, and asked Korvash to yield sword, shield and the key ring in view of the grey-cloaked scouts. He privately warned that the Foreman wants the mender too and that Ushk will escort the column to the Border Stones.

Day 19 ~1:45 PM: Korvash yielded sword, shield and key ring and was manacled by the Tallies; Ushk and ten spears are to escort the 94 children to Harrowmere via the Border Stones. Gorrak turns his column back toward Greyshaft with Korvash, letting the Foreman's scouts see the prisoner. Tessa signed back grey (hold, wait) instead of leaving.

Day 19 ~2-6 PM: marching north, Gorrak told Korvash privately: the Foreman keeps the chest key on a chain at his belt and never lends it; Gorrak's own name and his Tally debt are written in the master ledger; the Foreman will make an example of Korvash as a hand, sending him down the deep shaft with the ledger and the Tin Row's remnants. Gorrak plans a forced march by the old ore road to reach Greyshaft's lower gate at dusk on midwinter's eve (Day 20). He will not say what he intends. Column halts at dusk to camp by a rock shelter.

Day 19 ~5:50 PM: Korvash reminded him that his number burns with the book and that Korvash has already burned one ledger. Gorrak made no answer but did not rebuke him; he set his own cloak over a sleeping Korvash's shoulders? (No: he only turned the mask toward him a long moment and walked away.) Day 19 ~7:45 PM: Korvash heard, through the halt, Tessa's goat-counting song faintly from the rocks behind the shelter; she is trailing the column.

Day 19 night: during the climb Sergeant Dreg caught Korvash working at his manacles; he had a second cord tied from the chain to a guard's belt. Around 4 AM Day 20 Korvash saw a grey rag tied to a thorn at a switchback, with a scratched crescent on the stone below: Tessa's 'hold, I'm near' sign. Column still marching toward Greyshaft by the ore road; due at the lower gate at dusk.

Day 20 ~5:50 PM: on the ridge above Greyshaft, Korvash laid out the plan: present him before the Foreman near the chest, strike the cuffs off, and when Korvash moves for the key chain Gorrak either cuts the chain or cuts Korvash. Gorrak gave no promise but said 'Walk, then, and keep your hands low,' and led the column down to the lower gate.

Day 20 ~6:15 PM: when Korvash seized the Foreman and ripped the key chain from his belt, Gorrak cut the manacle chain and sided with him, shouting for his Tallies to hold; Stair Guards obeyed the Foreman instead. Gorrak is a veteran captain (ruling: 39 HP, AC 17); took 15 from a guard's Martial Advantage hit. Korvash dropped to 0 HP from a guard's blow (7).

Day 20 ~11:25 PM: Korvash glimpsed the scorched corner of the master ledger: Gorrak's debt line was once reduced to a small figure, then crossed out and re-inked much larger (his debt was effectively paid down about two winters ago and the Foreman inflated it again to keep him). Korvash alone knows; Gorrak does not. Foreman agreed to bind Gorrak's wounds.

Day 20 ~11:30 PM: Korvash announced aloud before the six Tally-sworn and Gorrak that the ledger shows Gorrak's debt reduced then re-inked. Persuasion 20 succeeded: the guards doubt; Gorrak heard and demanded the line be read.

Day 21 ~2:30 AM: held chained in the deep shaft beside Korvash after the ledger-house fight. Told Korvash the Foreman moved the scorched ledger to a chest on the third gate under his own grey-cloaks, and that Tessa was taken up the stair as the Foreman's mender. Several Tally-sworn asked him the number of his debt.

Day 21 dawn bell ~6:00 AM: Korvash roared the ledger truth through the shutters. The bell drowned most of it, but Dreg in the barracks yard caught it and shouted back for the page to be read. Gorrak and Krell stand under the gate beam with nooses ready; Foreman gagged Korvash and demanded the oath.

Day 21 morning: after Korvash's roar, Sergeant Dreg and Brun led the Tallies up the stair and held it; the hanging was stopped and Gorrak and Krell freed; the Foreman and his grey cloaks hold the barred ledger-house with Korvash and Tessa inside. Stalemate; parley through the door.

Day 21 ~5 PM: Gorrak commands Greyshaft with Dreg; has ordered all remaining captives (about thirty-eight children from the deep shaft and sixty-odd mine hands) released and readied to walk to Harrowmere at dawn under Korvash and Tessa with Dreg's escort. Korvash's oath is to continue after the meal at Veshra's.
Korvash's aunt in Harrowmere; raised him, sends word by travelers.

Day 1 evening: lives two streets from the market; sent Pell for Korvash. Told him a drover (Hale Orrin) saw the Iron Tallies' camp at Cinder Ford, below the Goat's Throat; a scout-pair watches the old herd track. She gives him a pouch of dried goat meat and a clan token: Dargan's whistle-carved horn charm. She will shelter Pell's family.
Young herder boy (about 12) in Harrowmere market, family shaken down by bullies. Carries word of a tin-masked hobgoblin captain with a notched rod seen on the high road, and a message from Veshra.
Pell's little sister (about 7), up with their uncle's flock near the Goat's Throat; feared taken by the Iron Tallies. Korvash gave his word to bring her home.

Day 2 evening, told Korvash: Gorrak counts the children each night with the rod, asks every child's name and which steading they are from. Asked Wren, gently, whether she'd seen a girl in a hooded cloak in the high rocks; she said no. Brakk the sergeant is cruel; Ushk gave her a blanket.

Korvash swore to Pell to bring his sister Wren home from the Iron Tallies camped below the Goat's Throat, where children are being taken from herding steadings. Korvash leaves for the pass tonight. The route leads to the pass where his father died and to the question of Tessa.
Done Day 3: Wren and all 31 children freed at the Border Stones and reunited with their families.
Stream crossing on the high road below the Goat's Throat; the Iron Tallies' camp, seen by drovers. Watched by hobgoblin scouts on the old herd track.

Day 2, ~2 AM: Korvash lost the goat-path (failed Survival) and came out on a scree shoulder about 300 yards from the ford, in view of the fires. The two scouts sit a rocky lookout upslope on the herd track.

Day 2, ~2:20 AM: Korvash's ambush on the scouts failed; the picket raised the alarm and Korvash fell at 0 HP. Ruling: the hobgoblins, on the picket's order ('the captain wants him alive for the rod'), stabilized him and took him captive into the Iron Tallies camp. Gorrak Vael is there. The archer (4 HP left) and picket (unhurt) live.

Day 2 dawn: Korvash swore on his father's blood to carry an axe for the Iron Tallies for a year and a day, in return for Gorrak Vael freeing all 31 children (including Wren) at Harrowmere's border stones. Gorrak promised Korvash's greataxe back at the stones. Korvash keeps his word. Wren's rescue now depends on the oath being honored; watch for Gorrak's treachery.

Day 21 ~2:20 PM: Korvash named the terms of his year and a day: free every captive in Greyshaft and walk them home, one meal at Veshra's table with Tessa, then he carries an axe wherever Gorrak asks for the rest of the term. Gorrak agreed to the captives and the meal; refused leave for Tally-sworn to desert freely.

Clan cairn at the Goat's Throat pass where Dargan fell. Day 2: Gorrak allowed Korvash to visit with a guard (a hobgoblin sergeant named Ushk). A small weathered goat figure of carved horn, with fresh ribbon of undyed wool, was left among the stones, recent, within a season; origin unknown (clue; do not confirm Tessa).

Natural 20 discovery: the underside of the horn goat bears Tessa's childhood lamb-mark (a notched crescent, her own design, which she cut into everything she owned). The ribbon is fresh wool; someone with the goat, or the goat's maker, visited within a season or two. Ushk (hobgoblin sergeant) says a small cloaked herder-girl or boy was seen at the cairn at dusk about two moons ago and bolted into the rocks; Gorrak ordered no hunt. Tessa's fate remains UNCONFIRMED.
Korvash put the goat back and scratched Tessa's crescent-mark into the base of the cairn with a message in Draconic: 'Tessa. Korvash lives. Harrowmere, Aunt Veshra's door.'

Day 11 ~1 AM (dark of the moon): Korvash lost the goat-path to the Weeping Ledge (failed Survival) and came out at the cairn. Beneath his scratched message, a new fresh scratch in Draconic: 'Not yet.' with the notched crescent. The horn goat is gone. Gorrak Vael waits at the cairn alone, unmasked at first glance, rod in hand.
Cruel hobgoblin sergeant of the Iron Tallies; kicked a boy on the stake line; Wren fears him. Ushk, by contrast, gave Wren an extra blanket.

Day 2 night: Korvash warned Ushk to keep Brakk off the children's line; Ushk posted Brakk on the far picket instead, with a grunt of agreement. Brakk glares at Korvash across the fold; has a ring in his ear.

Hobgoblin overseer of Greyshaft tin-mine, to whom Gorrak Vael owes a tally of 'hands' (children and axes) each season. Gorrak fears him; he will punish a short count. Korvash's sworn year-and-a-day axe is meant to cover part of Gorrak's quota. Learned by Korvash via natural 20 Insight on Day 2 night.

Day 14 morning: meets Korvash in the Counting House at Greyshaft's lowest gate. Heavy, fastidious hobgoblin in a leather apron with brass tallying beads on his belt and a ledger; speaks Common softly; never raises his voice. Has been told by his scouts that Korvash 'plays at sullen'. Asked what he was doing at his father's cairn on Day 11 (he knows via scouts). Assigns him to the second smelter gallery's door-guard, bunk in the lower barracks. Keeps the 'hands' ledger: names every laborer; a page for Korvash already prepared.

Day 14: believed the grief but sensed an omission (Deception 7). Assigned Korvash to the second smelter gallery door-guard, bunk in lower barracks, with a watcher bunkmate named Tally-Pip (young goblin, ledger-boy, reports to the Foreman). Declared the third gate off-limits to hired axes: 'the third gate is where the ledger sleeps.' Korvash must find a way up.

Day 20 ~6:10 PM (midwinter's eve): stands at the foot of the third-gate stair in the yard beside the iron-bound chest on a litter while the remaining Tin Row hands are marched to the deep shaft. Receives Gorrak's column and the manacled Korvash. Keys on a chain at his belt; brass beads in hand; soft voice. Two Tally-sworn carry the litter; six Tally-sworn guard the stair; grey-cloaked scouts on the wall.

Day 20 ~6:15 PM: wounded by Gorrak (7) and by Korvash's breath (2); at 2 HP, fled up the third-gate stair behind his guards and retook his key chain. His six Tally-sworn Stair Guards obeyed him over Gorrak.

Day 20 ~9:45 PM: holds Korvash, Tessa (both stable, knocked out in the deep shaft by guards) and Gorrak Vael (bound, mask removed) in his bedchamber in the ledger-house at the third gate. He is bandaged at the ribs, calm and polite, with the master ledger open on his desk and the iron-bound chest beside it, its lid scorched but unburned. He is writing Korvash and Tessa into the ledger as new hands. The 40 or so children remain chained in the deep shaft below; the Foreman means to seal the shaft and march them on at dawn.

Day 20 ~9:50 PM: Korvash laughed and defied him (Intimidation natural 1: the threat sounded hollow). The Foreman revealed he already knows the children went with Ushk's ten spears toward the Border Stones; his scouts counted them. He proposed a bargain: Korvash swears on Dargan's blood to serve Greyshaft as a hand until the ledger's count of ninety-four is made good (a debt measured by the Foreman), and in return Tessa is freed to go to Harrowmere with a safe-conduct and Gorrak's life is spared. He has a rider ready to take the grey cloaks to intercept Ushk if Korvash refuses. He knows Korvash 'keeps his word no matter what' and means to use it.

Day 20 ~9:55 PM: Counter-offer after Korvash demanded a fixed term (Persuasion 13, just missed): a year and a day for Greyshaft, but starting only when the Tallies' year and a day ends (so Korvash serves consecutively, about two years); Tessa's cords cut and a mule and safe-conduct at the oath, the rider recalled once the ink is dry; Gorrak Vael stays in the ledger as surety, released at the end of Korvash's term. Tessa is stirring awake and may speak against the bargain.

Day 20 ~10:05 PM: at Korvash's insistence he cut Tessa's cords and read the contract aloud. Clauses: (1) term a year and a day after the Tallies' term; (2) service wherever the Foreman sends; (3) 'the term runs only while the hand is whole and obedient': any day Korvash is disabled, disobedient or in flight is not counted (the trick Korvash caught: the term could be made endless); (4) Gorrak Vael is surety; (5) Tessa freed with a mule and safe-conduct once the oath is spoken. The Foreman, caught out, will concede clause 3 if Korvash points it out, grudgingly, because the ledger must be tidy.

Day 20 ~10:10 PM: heard Korvash's murmured Draconic (Insight beat Deception) and guessed a ploy; moved the lamp from Tessa and, when Korvash roared "HOME" and heaved at the table, snatched up the ledger. Tessa's thrown lamp (nat 1) smashed short and scorched the floor and the ledger's lower corner. Guards knocked Tessa and Korvash out with pommels. Foreman now holds Tessa as leverage; rider to Border Stones not recalled.

Day 20 ~11:30 PM: fight in the ledger-house. Korvash rammed the table into the Foreman; Guard Grey-eyes (grappled him) was killed by a loyal guard. Singed-beard and Tessa went for the ledger; it now lies open and smouldering on the stovetop. Gorrak read his own line aloud.

Day 21 ~3:00-3:40 AM: Foreman set a deadline: Korvash swears by the dawn bell or the rider goes to the Border Stones and Gorrak and Krell hang from the gate beam. Scorched ledger now in a new chest at his desk under a grey-cloak guard. Tessa sews at the stove, chained at one ankle. Gate-top layout seen by Korvash: wash-house roof door at the far end (one guard), the drain-stair behind it, two shuttered windows, ledger-house door barred from inside.

Day 21 ~4:30-5:50 AM: a grey cloak saw Korvash's clan signs (Stealth nat 1) and the Foreman read through the act (Insight 19 vs Deception 17). He found Tessa's shackle picked open, rechained her by the wrist to a ring behind his chair, took her needle, replaced the lamp with a shuttered lantern, and had the scorched ledger's chest carried into his inner bedchamber behind a barred door with two grey cloaks. Gorrak and Krell are being brought up to the gate beam for the dawn bell.

Day 21 ~9:58 AM: DEAD. Korvash smashed his lantern; burning oil caught his sleeve and killed him (he had 2 HP). Two loyal grey cloaks died to the Tallies' spears when Dreg's men broke in; four surrendered. The scorched ledger lies on his desk, key chain taken from his body by Tessa. Korvash was knocked down by a crossbow crit, stabilized by Tessa.

Three weathered standing stones marking Harrowmere's northern border on the high road, ten miles south of the drovers' fold. Day 3 ~11 AM: Aunt Veshra and about twenty armed herders and townsfolk of Harrowmere wait there, led by Veshra with Hale Orrin the drover; they intend to ambush the Tallies and free the children by force. This threatens the bargain.

Day 3 ~11 AM: Korvash's attempt to calm both sides partly failed. Gorrak cut the line's rope; children are being freed, but Veshra's party hasn't lowered weapons and Brakk, at the rear, has drawn a longbow on the villagers' archers.

Day 3 ~11 AM: Korvash grappled Brakk and pinned him; Ushk disarmed Brakk. Truce held. All 31 children freed to Harrowmere's villagers. Gorrak returned Korvash's greataxe, handaxes and javelins. Korvash is sworn to the Tallies for a year and a day; Gorrak has told him to report to the road at dawn on Day 4 at the stones.

Korvash's sister Tessa's fate is unknown. Clues: horn goat with her notched-crescent mark left at Dargan's cairn with fresh wool ribbon; a hooded small herder seen at the cairn two moons before Day 2 and spared by Gorrak's order; Gorrak notched then struck out a rod mark for an unaccounted girl of the clan and has shadowed no hunt. Korvash left a message at the cairn base. Gorrak will tell more at the Goat's Throat in the dark of the moon (about nine days).

Day 3-10: Veshra never had word from Tessa. Hobb Teyl says Dargan taught his children the Weeping Ledge shelter above the Throat. Town gossip (Persuasion 17): a salt-peddler named Marl Quill says a hooded girl twice left a bundle of goat-cheeses at the Seven Crooks inn's back step, paid in carved horn tokens, always at dusk, last seen four days before Day 3 heading up the high road.

Day 10: Korvash left word at the Seven Crooks (innkeeper and Marl Quill) for the hooded girl: 'Korvash lives. Veshra's door is open.' Day 11: at the cairn found a reply scratched beneath his own: 'Not yet.' with Tessa's crescent mark; the goat figure gone. Someone with Tessa's mark is alive and nearby, or was within days.

Day 11 dawn: after Korvash called into the dark in Draconic, nothing answered but he found at first light the horn goat on a flat stone on the east path, with a slate chip scratched in Draconic: 'Greyshaft. Third gate. Don't let him see you know me.' The writer is almost certainly Tessa or someone who knows her marks; the identity of 'him' is probably the Foreman or Gorrak. She will be at Greyshaft's third gate.

Day 11 morning: Korvash vowed not to show he knows her and tells no one, not even Gorrak. Heads for Greyshaft to arrive 'loud and sullen and bound by oath.' Third gate of Greyshaft is the meeting place. Midwinter's eve is the deadline.

Day 15 dusk: at the second gallery door, Korvash hears the hooded mender at the third-gate wash-line singing the clan's goat-counting song, the one Dargan sang; she hit the verse about the 'seventh goat that returns' twice, pointedly. The Foreman's guards did not notice. She has not looked down.

Day 16 dusk: Korvash hummed the answering lines; Pip wrote it down but accepted the sentiment. The mender answered with the wash-line: cloths hung grey, red, grey, an old clan field signal meaning 'meet by water after dark'. The third-gate wash-house sluice runs down to a stone culvert opening at the foot of the second wall, east side, behind the coal sheds; it is unguarded after the dusk bell except for a drunk pair on the wall above. Meeting set for after the second night bell.

DONE Day 16: Tessa found alive at Greyshaft's culvert. New purpose: help her break the Foreman's ledger and free the children in the lower galleries before midwinter's eve (Day 20), when the ledger and a hundred 'hands' move to the deep shaft.

Old goat-keeper in Harrowmere, once of Korvash's clan; knew the secret goat-paths and rock shelters around the Goat's Throat (including the Weeping Ledge, a cave behind a seep). Says Dargan taught the paths to both his children.
Hidden shelter in the rocks above the Goat's Throat behind a water seep; only clan members of Dargan's household knew it. Possible hiding place of the hooded figure.

Deadline for Korvash to report to Greyshaft's gate. DM ruling: it falls on Day 20, nine days after Day 11 (Day 11 = 5:58 AM when Korvash left the cairn). Greyshaft is three days' road from the Goat's Throat.

Pair of hobgoblin riders-on-foot in grey cloaks, sent by the Greyshaft Foreman to watch the road north of the Throat. Day 12 afternoon: Korvash spotted them on a ridge, shadowing him from half a mile off. They have not closed.

Day 12 night: Korvash's sullen act (Deception natural 1) overplayed: too loud, too much; the scouts doubt it. One of them ran ahead to Greyshaft to report he 'acts like a man with something to hide'; the other shadows him until the gate. The Foreman will have him watched.

Young goblin ledger-boy at Greyshaft, the Foreman's watcher assigned as Korvash's bunkmate; quick, bright-eyed, chatters; reports nightly to the Counting House. Can be bribed with rations or befriended.

Day 14 afternoon: befriended by Korvash with goat meat (Persuasion 13). Told him: shifts change at dawn, noon and dusk bells; water carts come at the noon bell; the guards of the second wall drink on watch after the dusk bell; the third gate is the Foreman's ledger-house and its stairs, guarded by six Tally-sworn hobgoblins, never drunk. A quiet girl, a mender 'who mends the ledger-bindings and sings to goats that aren't there', came with the autumn tally and sleeps in the ledger-house; Pip has only seen her at the gate-top wash-line at dusk. She wears a hood.
Day 21 ~5 PM: after the Foreman's death, Pip appeared at the ledger-house, shaken, asking where a ledger-boy goes when the ledger's gone; asked to come along to Harrowmere.
Day 21 evening: Korvash invited Pip to come to Harrowmere and keep Aunt Veshra's flour accounts, with a bunk at her table. Pip shared Korvash's bread.

Drunk hobgoblin guard of Greyshaft's second wall, east side. Day 16 night: spotted Korvash slipping toward the coal sheds and challenged him from the stair; half-drunk, loud, curious, loyal to the Foreman's coin more than the Foreman.

Day 16 night: accepted Korvash's insomnia excuse and a strip of goat meat (Deception 11, just). Told him: 'Don't let the Foreman's boys see you east of the sheds after the bell, Emberhide. I never saw you.' Returned to the wall to drink with his mate. Owes Korvash nothing but will not volunteer the sighting unless asked.

Korvash's younger sister, alive. Day 16 night, ~10:30 PM, met him at the Greyshaft culvert. Small and wiry for a dragonborn, red scales dulled to rust, left horn broken, burn scar on one forearm; hooded; speaks Draconic in short clipped sentences; she cut her crescent mark. Survived the raid by hiding on the Weeping Ledge as a child; Dargan's cairn-stones hid her; Gorrak let her go. Lived in the rocks and as a goat-girl on far farms; took the mender's post at Greyshaft on purpose, one autumn ago, to learn the ledger. Wants to free the children held in the lower galleries and destroy the Foreman's ledger of 'hands'.

Clan cloth signals (Dargan's fold): grey alone = fair weather, nothing to report, hold the plan; grey-red-grey = meet at the stream after dark, come alone; red alone (single) = go now / the way is open. Day 18 dusk: three greys at the gate-top, then a single red cloth hung after Korvash tied his red thread.

Day 19 ~7:15 AM: Asked whether Gorrak Vael will be ally or the Foreman's, she said honestly she does not know: he let her go the night of the raid, but he fears the Foreman and the ledger counts him too. Day 19 ~8:10 AM: column reached the stream at the foot of the east track; Korvash chose to halt and wait for Vael there.

Day 20 ~4 AM: Korvash scuffed a message in Draconic under her crescent on the ore road ('Dusk. Lower gate. Ledger moves. Gorrak's number burns with it.') unseen by the Tallies. Column reaches Greyshaft's lower gate ~6 PM Day 20 after a day-long march with short halts.

Day 20 ~7:30 PM: Korvash hummed the goat-counting song in the deep shaft, unnoticed by guards. A faint answering three taps came from the rock behind the far wall of the gallery, in the rhythm of the counting song. A child said Gorrak was dragged up the third-gate stair by two grey cloaks; no one saw a hooded girl taken.

Day 20 ~7:40 PM: she answered Korvash's tapping from a seam in the deep shaft's far wall, opening it a crack to reach the shackle locks; her first pick attempt scraped loudly (7 vs 15). A guard with a singed beard picked up a torch and walked the row to look.
Day 20 ~7:41 PM: Korvash's feigned fever failed (nat 1, too theatrical); the singed-beard guard stopped just out of chain reach and spotted the lock-pick and a hooded shape against the wall.

Day 20 ~7:41 PM: dropped to 0 HP fighting the chest guards in the deep shaft (a child pile-on tripped a guard; she stabilized Korvash with Medicine 14). The guard knocked her out, stable; captured. ~9:45 PM: lies bound beside Korvash in the Foreman's bedchamber.

With Tessa, destroy the Greyshaft Foreman's ledger of 'hands' and free the children held in the lower galleries before Day 20 (midwinter's eve), when the ledger and about a hundred laborers are moved to the deep shaft. Complications: Korvash's year-and-a-day oath to the Iron Tallies; Gorrak Vael's debt and fear; Tally-Pip watches Korvash; third gate guarded by six Tally-sworn hobgoblins.

Day 16 night, Tessa's intel: the ledger-house crowns the third gate; six Tally-sworn hobgoblins hold the stair in two shifts of three (changing at the dusk bell and the dawn bell); a wash-house door on the gate-top roof is unlocked from inside by Tessa and opens onto the Foreman's outer room. The ledger sleeps in an iron-bound chest in the Foreman's bedchamber; the key is on a chain at his belt and he sleeps lightly. A second ledger, the copy, is in the Counting House by the lower gate. Plan window: the nights of Day 18 or 19, before the move on Day 20. Tessa can open the wash-house door any night at the second bell; Korvash can reach the gate-top roof via the sluice path and the wash-house drain-stair.

Plan agreed Day 16 night: night of Day 18: Korvash burns the copy in the Counting House first (he'll pull it from the shelf), then climbs the drain-stair to the third gate and Tessa lets him in at the second bell to burn the master ledger. Children are held in the Tin Row, a barred bunkhouse built into the cliff beneath the first gate (two hundred feet below the Counting House), 94 children, kept by Warden Hask and four wall-guards; its door key is on the Foreman's chain, but the Tin Row also has an old ore-chute at its back that Tessa has found, leading out to the scree on the east side. Signal: Korvash hangs a red thread on his belt at dusk on Day 18 if the way is clear. Tessa lamp-oil stash under the wash-house. Pip must be kept fed and bored.

Day 18 night: Korvash set fire to the east coal shed but his Stealth failed (6) and a Counting House door guard saw him; the alarm is rising. Night scribe still inside with the copy. Guard 2 ran to the fire; the second bell has not yet rung.

Day 18 ~6:08 PM: Korvash set the Counting House copy and shelves alight with the lamp oil; copy burning. The master ledger in the third-gate ledger-house remains. Korvash is at 2 HP in a burning room, the doorway held by Guard 1; second wall's torches closing.

Day 18 ~8:10 PM: Korvash fell at 0 HP in the burning Counting House; the Foreman's guards stabilized him (the Foreman wants him alive as a 'hand') and put the fire out, saving the shelves but not the copy ledger, which is ash. He is held in the Tin Row with the children, stripped of axe, handaxes, javelins, pouch (coins, Tessa's horn goat and slate chip), all taken to the Foreman. The Foreman may now know of a link to the mender (Tessa). Tessa will hear the alarm. Master ledger intact in the ledger-house. Midwinter's eve move is in two days.

Day 19 ~6:25 AM: Korvash tore out the Tin Row ore-chute grate frame (nat 20) and found behind it an old side-drift with rusted rails and a ladder rising toward the third gate, smelling of lamp oil and paper; Tessa's crescent is scratched on a rivet where she sawed it over nights. Tin Row door locked and wedged with a stool leg; Sentry A and B outside.

Day 19 ~6:30 AM: Korvash got out through the chute with the last children to the east scree to Tessa; sentries A and B raised the alarm; all 94 children free of the Row but pursuit expected. Master ledger still in the ledger-house; Korvash has 2 HP, no lamp oil, longsword and shield only.

Day 19 ~6:50 AM: Tessa leads 94 children down the east goat-track gully with Ninna counting; Korvash's slate-pull failed (12) and only half the slope came down; two of the Foreman's grey-cloaked scouts have caught up on the ridge above the gully.

Day 19 ~7:10 AM: Korvash's nat-20 Intimidation unnerved the two scouts; they backed off and one let slip the Foreman ordered them to follow and count, not fight, and that a rider already went to Gorrak Vael at Cinder Ford: Vael will be on the road by dusk. Scouts shadow the column from afar.

Day 20 ~6:10 PM (midwinter's eve): at the lower-gate yard, Korvash grappled the Foreman and tore off the key chain; Gorrak cut his chain and sided with him but the six Stair Guards obeyed the Foreman. Korvash dropped to 0, rose on a nat-20 death save, breathed fire (Foreman now 2 HP, two guards at 6 HP, litter scorched but ledger chest intact), then was knocked out (stable) by Guard 2. Gorrak lies knocked out and bleeding. The Foreman retook the keys and fled up the stair. Day 20 ~7:10 PM: Korvash wakes shackled in the deep shaft with the Tin Row's remnants; the chest was carried down too. Tessa's red cloth was the 'go' signal; her whereabouts unknown.

Day 21 ~2 PM: the Foreman is dead; the scorched master ledger sits on his desk in the ledger-house, under Gorrak's and Dreg's eyes; Tessa has the key chain. Korvash has not yet burned it; decision pending (Gorrak's debt is in it, along with the Tallies' tallies). Oath to the Tallies still stands unless Gorrak releases it.

Day 21 ~2 PM: Korvash burned the master ledger page by page in the ledger-house stove before the Tallies in the doorway. Quest accomplished. Gorrak accepted freeing all captives in Greyshaft and a meal at Veshra's, but refused (Persuasion nat 1) that Tally-sworn may leave freely at will; Tally-sworn answer to him.
Hobgoblin warden of the Tin Row, the barred bunkhouse where Greyshaft's captive children sleep; keeps four wall-guards. Methodical, joyless, drinks nothing. Carries a ring of keys.

Day 18 night: took custody of Korvash in the Tin Row on the Foreman's orders; chained him by one ankle to a ring at the end of the row beside the children. Methodical, took his belt and pouch to the Foreman.

Day 19 ~5:55 AM: choked unconscious by Korvash, bound and gagged with blanket strips. Four wall-guards of the Tin Row were bound asleep with rope. Korvash holds the key ring. The Tin Row is unlocked but still unnoticed from outside (dawn bell has just rung).

About ten years old, in the Tin Row at Greyshaft; unsurprised, shrewd, a herders' daughter from the lower steadings. Told Korvash (Day 18 night): the ore-chute at the back is a cellar-hatch fifteen paces behind the last bunk, a square iron grate bolted from the outside, wide enough for ten-year-olds; the older ones won't fit. A hooded mender came two nights ago with bread and told the children to 'wait until a goat sings.' Hask keeps all keys on the ring in his lap, including the one for Korvash's manacle; he counts the children each dawn and dusk and sleeps at his stool in shifts with four wall-guards at the door.

Day 19 pre-dawn: agreed with Korvash to have the smallest children loosen the chute-grate nuts at dawn if they can, to cough and moan about the 'dying' man at the dawn count, and to wait for the mender's goat-song. Korvash rested the night (long rest, undisturbed).

Day 19 ~6:20 AM: organized the children in tens at the chute, littlest first, older carrying the little ones. About thirty were out onto the east scree when a wall sentry noticed. Tessa's goat-song is heard from outside.

Tally-sworn guard of the Greyshaft ledger-house, the one with the singed beard (Korvash burned it Day 20). Turned against the Foreman when Gorrak read his debt line aloud; fought Guard 3 and was struck down. Held in the deep shaft with Korvash and Gorrak.
Day 21 ~2:35 AM: gave his name to Korvash; twelve years in Greyshaft, knows the stair guards' shifts. Wounded: split head, swollen arm.
Tally-sworn stair guard (the fifth guard, who dropped his sword when Gorrak read the ledger line). Young, frightened of the Foreman, but one of the four who asked Gorrak his number.

Day 21 ~2:40 AM: was the farther of the two spearmen at the deep-shaft door; flinched at his name but said nothing. The nearer spearman (a grey-cloak) overheard Korvash's whisper about Dreg and the dawn bell and reported it up the stair.
Day 21 morning: sided with Dreg and Gorrak's Tallies in storming the stair.
Sheltered hollow with a spring beside the ore road, a day's slow walk below Greyshaft. The freed column camped here on Day 22 night. Harrowmere is about another day's walk beyond.

sheet.name: Korvash Emberhide
sheet.opening: Korvash Emberhide, a hulking red-scaled dragonborn barbarian (Chaotic Good, loud, proud, quick to anger; ideal Charity; bond: he keeps his word no matter what; flaw: inflexible), arrives at dusk in a lowland market town near the foot of the mountains, driving off a pack of bullies shaking down a family of herders, as he has done for years. His past, which the opening must respect: he comes from a clan of mountain herders. When he was young, hobgoblins of the Iron Tallies warband, led by a tin-masked captain named Gorrak Vael (who notches a rod for every raid), overran his village. His father Dargan held the narrow Goat's Throat pass, losing a hand and then his life, so the herd and the children could flee; Korvash swore to him, with his blood on his hands, to protect the weak. His younger sister Tessa was lost in the raid and her fate is UNKNOWN: he never saw her fall and has never stopped wondering, so she must not be confirmed alive or dead unless discovered in play. The survivors fled to Harrowmere, where his aunt Veshra raised him and still sends word by travelers. The clan built a cairn at the Goat's Throat, which he has never had the heart to revisit. His shame at being too young to stand beside his father is why he is loud and makes sure everyone knows he is standing. He carries his father's second-best greataxe with Dargan's ember-red scale-sash tied to the haft. Hook for the opening: just after the bullies flee, a frightened young herder or a traveler brings him word, perhaps carried from Aunt Veshra, that a hobgoblin warband bearing a tin-masked captain and a notched rod has been seen again, or that something connected to the Goat's Throat has turned up. This pulls him toward an oath-bound choice: someone weak is in immediate danger, he promises to help, and keeping that word will lead him back toward the mountains and the questions about Tessa. Invent only original places and people; keep it grounded in the SRD's monsters (hobgoblins, goblins, bugbears, wolves, etc.).

I can't stand to see someone weaker get pushed around.

personality.bond: I keep my word no matter what.
personality.flaw: I am inflexible in my thinking.

features: Draconic Ancestry: You have draconic ancestry. Choose one type of dragon from the Draconic Ancestry table. Your breath weapon and damage resistance are determined by the dragon type, as shown in the table.

Breath Weapon: You can use your action to exhale destructive energy. Your draconic ancestry determines the size, shape, and damage type of the exhalation. When you use your breath weapon, each creature in the area of the exhalation must make a saving throw, the type of which is determined by your draconic ancestry. The DC for this saving throw equals 8 + your Constitution modifier + your proficiency bonus. A creature takes 2d6 damage on a failed save, and half as much damage on a successful one. The damage increases to 3d6 at 6th level, 4d6 at 11th level, and 5d6 at 16th level. After you use your breath weapon, you cannot use it again until you complete a short or long rest.
Damage Resistance: You have resistance to the damage type associated with your draconic ancestry.
Draconic Ancestry (Red): breath weapon 15 ft cone, DEX save DC 12, 2d6 Fire damage (half on a success); resistance to that damage type

Rage: In battle, you fight with primal ferocity. On your turn, you can enter a rage as a bonus action. While raging, you gain the following benefits if you aren't wearing heavy armor: - You have advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws. - When you make a melee weapon attack using Strength, you gain a bonus to the damage roll that increases as you gain levels as a barbarian, as shown in the Rage Damage column of the Barbarian table. - You have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage. If you are able to cast spells, you can't cast them or concentrate on them while raging. Your rage lasts for 1 minute. It ends early if you are knocked unconscious or if your turn ends and you haven't attacked a hostile creature since your last turn or taken damage since then. You can also end your rage on your turn as a bonus action. Once you have raged the number of times shown for your barbarian level in the Rages column of the Barbarian table, you must finish a long rest before you can rage again. At level 2: rage damage bonus +2; 2 rages before a long rest.
Unarmored Defense: While you are not wearing any armor, your Armor Class equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Constitution modifier. You can use a shield and still gain this benefit.

Reckless Attack: Starting at 2nd level, you can throw aside all concern for defense to attack with fierce desperation. When you make your first attack on your turn, you can decide to attack recklessly. Doing so gives you advantage on melee weapon attack rolls using Strength during this turn, but attack rolls against you have advantage until your next turn.

Danger Sense: At 2nd level, you gain an uncanny sense of when things nearby aren't as they should be, giving you an edge when you dodge away from danger. You have advantage on Dexterity saving throws against effects that you can see, such as traps and spells. To gain this benefit, you can't be blinded, deafened, or incapacitated.

Shelter of the Faithful (Acolyte): As an acolyte, you command the respect of those who share your faith, and you can perform the religious ceremonies of your deity. You and your adventuring companions can expect to receive free healing and care at a temple, shrine, or other established presence of your faith, though you must provide any material components needed for spells. Those who share your religion will support you (but only you) at a modest lifestyle. You might also have ties to a specific temple dedicated to your chosen deity or pantheon, and you have a residence there. This could be the temple where you used to serve, if you remain on good terms with it, or a temple where you have found a new home. While near your temple, you can call upon the priests for assistance, provided the assistance you ask for is not hazardous and you remain in good standing with your temple.

description.text: Lowland market town near the foot of the mountains. Korvash's clan fled here; his aunt Veshra raised him here.
Tin-masked hobgoblin captain of the Iron Tallies warband; notches a rod for every raid. Overran Korvash's village.
Day 2: his hobgoblins captured Korvash at Cinder Ford. Korvash's greataxe (with Dargan's sash), handaxes and javelins were taken and are kept in the camp's baggage pile near the captain's tent.

Day 2 dawn: speaks Common, calm and dry. Offers Korvash a bargain: swear on his word to serve the Iron Tallies as a hired axe for one year and one day, and the children go free to Harrowmere. Knows Dargan's name and recognized the ember-red sash. Wears a tin mask; has both hands (Dargan did not take his hand; Dargan lost his own).

Refused to free the children before Korvash swears; counter-offer: Korvash swears now, then walks with the line under escort to Harrowmere's border, where the children are cut loose. Korvash's cord is secretly parted behind his back (Day 2, 5:18 AM).
Day 2: accepted Korvash's oath. Wants him at the head of the line. Axe returns at the border stones. Has told Korvash to rest first; camp breaks around noon.
Two moons before Day 2 he ordered his patrol NOT to hunt the small cloaked figure seen at Dargan's cairn. Reason unknown.

Day 2 noon: Asked why he spared the figure at the cairn, he said: 'Some marks on my rod are not for notching. You'll have the answer at the stones, with your axe in your hand.' Deferred. Marches the line south toward Harrowmere's border stones; first night's halt at an abandoned drovers' fold.

Day 2 night, in his tent: told Korvash (truthfully) that at the Goat's Throat he offered Dargan the children's lives for the axe, and Dargan refused. After the raid one child of the clan was never accounted for on his count; he notched the rod for her, then struck it out. He does not know whether the hooded figure is Tessa. He has never hunted it and wants it found by no one else. Insight natural 20: he is afraid of the Greyshaft Foreman, owes him a quota, and freeing the children short-counts him; Korvash's oath was meant to cover the shortfall. He will keep his word to free the children anyway.

Day 11 ~1 AM at the cairn: says he arrived just after the fresh cuts were made; the figure was gone. Admits he saw a small figure slip through the goat-path while Dargan held the Throat and let her go, a debt to Dargan, and has watched for her since to keep the Foreman's scouts from finding her. Greyshaft wants a dragonborn axe-and-fire for the smelter galleries; Korvash is to report to Greyshaft's gate by midwinter's eve. Gorrak offers: leave at dawn, three days' road.

Day 19 ~1:10 PM: met Korvash's column on the high road beyond the stream with about twenty Iron Tally hobgoblins; halted his column and came forward with Sergeant Ushk, rod in hand. Foreman's scouts shadow the column from the ridges.

Day 19 ~1:20 PM: Korvash met him alone on the road and pleaded for the children's passage (Persuasion 6, failed). Gorrak did not refuse outright but said he cannot let ninety-four short-counted hands walk past with the Foreman's riders watching; he demands Korvash's year-and-a-day oath be honored now, in exchange for a delay. Ushk uneasy. Terms are not yet settled.

Day 19 ~1:25 PM: Korvash stepped up and told him privately that the girl he let go over the ledge is in the ditch, then publicly offered himself, his axe and his year-and-a-day to be taken to Greyshaft if the children go free. Gorrak was shaken by the mention of Tessa, accepted the trade in principle, and asked Korvash to yield sword, shield and the key ring in view of the grey-cloaked scouts. He privately warned that the Foreman wants the mender too and that Ushk will escort the column to the Border Stones.

Day 19 ~1:45 PM: Korvash yielded sword, shield and key ring and was manacled by the Tallies; Ushk and ten spears are to escort the 94 children to Harrowmere via the Border Stones. Gorrak turns his column back toward Greyshaft with Korvash, letting the Foreman's scouts see the prisoner. Tessa signed back grey (hold, wait) instead of leaving.

Day 19 ~2-6 PM: marching north, Gorrak told Korvash privately: the Foreman keeps the chest key on a chain at his belt and never lends it; Gorrak's own name and his Tally debt are written in the master ledger; the Foreman will make an example of Korvash as a hand, sending him down the deep shaft with the ledger and the Tin Row's remnants. Gorrak plans a forced march by the old ore road to reach Greyshaft's lower gate at dusk on midwinter's eve (Day 20). He will not say what he intends. Column halts at dusk to camp by a rock shelter.

Day 19 ~5:50 PM: Korvash reminded him that his number burns with the book and that Korvash has already burned one ledger. Gorrak made no answer but did not rebuke him; he set his own cloak over a sleeping Korvash's shoulders? (No: he only turned the mask toward him a long moment and walked away.) Day 19 ~7:45 PM: Korvash heard, through the halt, Tessa's goat-counting song faintly from the rocks behind the shelter; she is trailing the column.

Day 19 night: during the climb Sergeant Dreg caught Korvash working at his manacles; he had a second cord tied from the chain to a guard's belt. Around 4 AM Day 20 Korvash saw a grey rag tied to a thorn at a switchback, with a scratched crescent on the stone below: Tessa's 'hold, I'm near' sign. Column still marching toward Greyshaft by the ore road; due at the lower gate at dusk.

Day 20 ~5:50 PM: on the ridge above Greyshaft, Korvash laid out the plan: present him before the Foreman near the chest, strike the cuffs off, and when Korvash moves for the key chain Gorrak either cuts the chain or cuts Korvash. Gorrak gave no promise but said 'Walk, then, and keep your hands low,' and led the column down to the lower gate.

Day 20 ~6:15 PM: when Korvash seized the Foreman and ripped the key chain from his belt, Gorrak cut the manacle chain and sided with him, shouting for his Tallies to hold; Stair Guards obeyed the Foreman instead. Gorrak is a veteran captain (ruling: 39 HP, AC 17); took 15 from a guard's Martial Advantage hit. Korvash dropped to 0 HP from a guard's blow (7).

Day 20 ~11:25 PM: Korvash glimpsed the scorched corner of the master ledger: Gorrak's debt line was once reduced to a small figure, then crossed out and re-inked much larger (his debt was effectively paid down about two winters ago and the Foreman inflated it again to keep him). Korvash alone knows; Gorrak does not. Foreman agreed to bind Gorrak's wounds.

Day 20 ~11:30 PM: Korvash announced aloud before the six Tally-sworn and Gorrak that the ledger shows Gorrak's debt reduced then re-inked. Persuasion 20 succeeded: the guards doubt; Gorrak heard and demanded the line be read.

Day 21 ~2:30 AM: held chained in the deep shaft beside Korvash after the ledger-house fight. Told Korvash the Foreman moved the scorched ledger to a chest on the third gate under his own grey-cloaks, and that Tessa was taken up the stair as the Foreman's mender. Several Tally-sworn asked him the number of his debt.

Day 21 dawn bell ~6:00 AM: Korvash roared the ledger truth through the shutters. The bell drowned most of it, but Dreg in the barracks yard caught it and shouted back for the page to be read. Gorrak and Krell stand under the gate beam with nooses ready; Foreman gagged Korvash and demanded the oath.

Day 21 morning: after Korvash's roar, Sergeant Dreg and Brun led the Tallies up the stair and held it; the hanging was stopped and Gorrak and Krell freed; the Foreman and his grey cloaks hold the barred ledger-house with Korvash and Tessa inside. Stalemate; parley through the door.

Day 21 ~5 PM: Gorrak commands Greyshaft with Dreg; has ordered all remaining captives (about thirty-eight children from the deep shaft and sixty-odd mine hands) released and readied to walk to Harrowmere at dawn under Korvash and Tessa with Dreg's escort. Korvash's oath is to continue after the meal at Veshra's.
Korvash's aunt in Harrowmere; raised him, sends word by travelers.

Day 1 evening: lives two streets from the market; sent Pell for Korvash. Told him a drover (Hale Orrin) saw the Iron Tallies' camp at Cinder Ford, below the Goat's Throat; a scout-pair watches the old herd track. She gives him a pouch of dried goat meat and a clan token: Dargan's whistle-carved horn charm. She will shelter Pell's family.
Young herder boy (about 12) in Harrowmere market, family shaken down by bullies. Carries word of a tin-masked hobgoblin captain with a notched rod seen on the high road, and a message from Veshra.
Pell's little sister (about 7), up with their uncle's flock near the Goat's Throat; feared taken by the Iron Tallies. Korvash gave his word to bring her home.

Day 2 evening, told Korvash: Gorrak counts the children each night with the rod, asks every child's name and which steading they are from. Asked Wren, gently, whether she'd seen a girl in a hooded cloak in the high rocks; she said no. Brakk the sergeant is cruel; Ushk gave her a blanket.

Korvash swore to Pell to bring his sister Wren home from the Iron Tallies camped below the Goat's Throat, where children are being taken from herding steadings. Korvash leaves for the pass tonight. The route leads to the pass where his father died and to the question of Tessa.
Done Day 3: Wren and all 31 children freed at the Border Stones and reunited with their families.
Stream crossing on the high road below the Goat's Throat; the Iron Tallies' camp, seen by drovers. Watched by hobgoblin scouts on the old herd track.

Day 2, ~2 AM: Korvash lost the goat-path (failed Survival) and came out on a scree shoulder about 300 yards from the ford, in view of the fires. The two scouts sit a rocky lookout upslope on the herd track.

Day 2, ~2:20 AM: Korvash's ambush on the scouts failed; the picket raised the alarm and Korvash fell at 0 HP. Ruling: the hobgoblins, on the picket's order ('the captain wants him alive for the rod'), stabilized him and took him captive into the Iron Tallies camp. Gorrak Vael is there. The archer (4 HP left) and picket (unhurt) live.

Day 2 dawn: Korvash swore on his father's blood to carry an axe for the Iron Tallies for a year and a day, in return for Gorrak Vael freeing all 31 children (including Wren) at Harrowmere's border stones. Gorrak promised Korvash's greataxe back at the stones. Korvash keeps his word. Wren's rescue now depends on the oath being honored; watch for Gorrak's treachery.

Day 21 ~2:20 PM: Korvash named the terms of his year and a day: free every captive in Greyshaft and walk them home, one meal at Veshra's table with Tessa, then he carries an axe wherever Gorrak asks for the rest of the term. Gorrak agreed to the captives and the meal; refused leave for Tally-sworn to desert freely.

Clan cairn at the Goat's Throat pass where Dargan fell. Day 2: Gorrak allowed Korvash to visit with a guard (a hobgoblin sergeant named Ushk). A small weathered goat figure of carved horn, with fresh ribbon of undyed wool, was left among the stones, recent, within a season; origin unknown (clue; do not confirm Tessa).

Natural 20 discovery: the underside of the horn goat bears Tessa's childhood lamb-mark (a notched crescent, her own design, which she cut into everything she owned). The ribbon is fresh wool; someone with the goat, or the goat's maker, visited within a season or two. Ushk (hobgoblin sergeant) says a small cloaked herder-girl or boy was seen at the cairn at dusk about two moons ago and bolted into the rocks; Gorrak ordered no hunt. Tessa's fate remains UNCONFIRMED.
Korvash put the goat back and scratched Tessa's crescent-mark into the base of the cairn with a message in Draconic: 'Tessa. Korvash lives. Harrowmere, Aunt Veshra's door.'

Day 11 ~1 AM (dark of the moon): Korvash lost the goat-path to the Weeping Ledge (failed Survival) and came out at the cairn. Beneath his scratched message, a new fresh scratch in Draconic: 'Not yet.' with the notched crescent. The horn goat is gone. Gorrak Vael waits at the cairn alone, unmasked at first glance, rod in hand.
Cruel hobgoblin sergeant of the Iron Tallies; kicked a boy on the stake line; Wren fears him. Ushk, by contrast, gave Wren an extra blanket.

Day 2 night: Korvash warned Ushk to keep Brakk off the children's line; Ushk posted Brakk on the far picket instead, with a grunt of agreement. Brakk glares at Korvash across the fold; has a ring in his ear.

Hobgoblin overseer of Greyshaft tin-mine, to whom Gorrak Vael owes a tally of 'hands' (children and axes) each season. Gorrak fears him; he will punish a short count. Korvash's sworn year-and-a-day axe is meant to cover part of Gorrak's quota. Learned by Korvash via natural 20 Insight on Day 2 night.

Day 14 morning: meets Korvash in the Counting House at Greyshaft's lowest gate. Heavy, fastidious hobgoblin in a leather apron with brass tallying beads on his belt and a ledger; speaks Common softly; never raises his voice. Has been told by his scouts that Korvash 'plays at sullen'. Asked what he was doing at his father's cairn on Day 11 (he knows via scouts). Assigns him to the second smelter gallery's door-guard, bunk in the lower barracks. Keeps the 'hands' ledger: names every laborer; a page for Korvash already prepared.

Day 14: believed the grief but sensed an omission (Deception 7). Assigned Korvash to the second smelter gallery door-guard, bunk in lower barracks, with a watcher bunkmate named Tally-Pip (young goblin, ledger-boy, reports to the Foreman). Declared the third gate off-limits to hired axes: 'the third gate is where the ledger sleeps.' Korvash must find a way up.

Day 20 ~6:10 PM (midwinter's eve): stands at the foot of the third-gate stair in the yard beside the iron-bound chest on a litter while the remaining Tin Row hands are marched to the deep shaft. Receives Gorrak's column and the manacled Korvash. Keys on a chain at his belt; brass beads in hand; soft voice. Two Tally-sworn carry the litter; six Tally-sworn guard the stair; grey-cloaked scouts on the wall.

Day 20 ~6:15 PM: wounded by Gorrak (7) and by Korvash's breath (2); at 2 HP, fled up the third-gate stair behind his guards and retook his key chain. His six Tally-sworn Stair Guards obeyed him over Gorrak.

Day 20 ~9:45 PM: holds Korvash, Tessa (both stable, knocked out in the deep shaft by guards) and Gorrak Vael (bound, mask removed) in his bedchamber in the ledger-house at the third gate. He is bandaged at the ribs, calm and polite, with the master ledger open on his desk and the iron-bound chest beside it, its lid scorched but unburned. He is writing Korvash and Tessa into the ledger as new hands. The 40 or so children remain chained in the deep shaft below; the Foreman means to seal the shaft and march them on at dawn.

Day 20 ~9:50 PM: Korvash laughed and defied him (Intimidation natural 1: the threat sounded hollow). The Foreman revealed he already knows the children went with Ushk's ten spears toward the Border Stones; his scouts counted them. He proposed a bargain: Korvash swears on Dargan's blood to serve Greyshaft as a hand until the ledger's count of ninety-four is made good (a debt measured by the Foreman), and in return Tessa is freed to go to Harrowmere with a safe-conduct and Gorrak's life is spared. He has a rider ready to take the grey cloaks to intercept Ushk if Korvash refuses. He knows Korvash 'keeps his word no matter what' and means to use it.

Day 20 ~9:55 PM: Counter-offer after Korvash demanded a fixed term (Persuasion 13, just missed): a year and a day for Greyshaft, but starting only when the Tallies' year and a day ends (so Korvash serves consecutively, about two years); Tessa's cords cut and a mule and safe-conduct at the oath, the rider recalled once the ink is dry; Gorrak Vael stays in the ledger as surety, released at the end of Korvash's term. Tessa is stirring awake and may speak against the bargain.

Day 20 ~10:05 PM: at Korvash's insistence he cut Tessa's cords and read the contract aloud. Clauses: (1) term a year and a day after the Tallies' term; (2) service wherever the Foreman sends; (3) 'the term runs only while the hand is whole and obedient': any day Korvash is disabled, disobedient or in flight is not counted (the trick Korvash caught: the term could be made endless); (4) Gorrak Vael is surety; (5) Tessa freed with a mule and safe-conduct once the oath is spoken. The Foreman, caught out, will concede clause 3 if Korvash points it out, grudgingly, because the ledger must be tidy.

Day 20 ~10:10 PM: heard Korvash's murmured Draconic (Insight beat Deception) and guessed a ploy; moved the lamp from Tessa and, when Korvash roared "HOME" and heaved at the table, snatched up the ledger. Tessa's thrown lamp (nat 1) smashed short and scorched the floor and the ledger's lower corner. Guards knocked Tessa and Korvash out with pommels. Foreman now holds Tessa as leverage; rider to Border Stones not recalled.

Day 20 ~11:30 PM: fight in the ledger-house. Korvash rammed the table into the Foreman; Guard Grey-eyes (grappled him) was killed by a loyal guard. Singed-beard and Tessa went for the ledger; it now lies open and smouldering on the stovetop. Gorrak read his own line aloud.

Day 21 ~3:00-3:40 AM: Foreman set a deadline: Korvash swears by the dawn bell or the rider goes to the Border Stones and Gorrak and Krell hang from the gate beam. Scorched ledger now in a new chest at his desk under a grey-cloak guard. Tessa sews at the stove, chained at one ankle. Gate-top layout seen by Korvash: wash-house roof door at the far end (one guard), the drain-stair behind it, two shuttered windows, ledger-house door barred from inside.

Day 21 ~4:30-5:50 AM: a grey cloak saw Korvash's clan signs (Stealth nat 1) and the Foreman read through the act (Insight 19 vs Deception 17). He found Tessa's shackle picked open, rechained her by the wrist to a ring behind his chair, took her needle, replaced the lamp with a shuttered lantern, and had the scorched ledger's chest carried into his inner bedchamber behind a barred door with two grey cloaks. Gorrak and Krell are being brought up to the gate beam for the dawn bell.

Day 21 ~9:58 AM: DEAD. Korvash smashed his lantern; burning oil caught his sleeve and killed him (he had 2 HP). Two loyal grey cloaks died to the Tallies' spears when Dreg's men broke in; four surrendered. The scorched ledger lies on his desk, key chain taken from his body by Tessa. Korvash was knocked down by a crossbow crit, stabilized by Tessa.

Three weathered standing stones marking Harrowmere's northern border on the high road, ten miles south of the drovers' fold. Day 3 ~11 AM: Aunt Veshra and about twenty armed herders and townsfolk of Harrowmere wait there, led by Veshra with Hale Orrin the drover; they intend to ambush the Tallies and free the children by force. This threatens the bargain.

Day 3 ~11 AM: Korvash's attempt to calm both sides partly failed. Gorrak cut the line's rope; children are being freed, but Veshra's party hasn't lowered weapons and Brakk, at the rear, has drawn a longbow on the villagers' archers.

Day 3 ~11 AM: Korvash grappled Brakk and pinned him; Ushk disarmed Brakk. Truce held. All 31 children freed to Harrowmere's villagers. Gorrak returned Korvash's greataxe, handaxes and javelins. Korvash is sworn to the Tallies for a year and a day; Gorrak has told him to report to the road at dawn on Day 4 at the stones.

Korvash's sister Tessa's fate is unknown. Clues: horn goat with her notched-crescent mark left at Dargan's cairn with fresh wool ribbon; a hooded small herder seen at the cairn two moons before Day 2 and spared by Gorrak's order; Gorrak notched then struck out a rod mark for an unaccounted girl of the clan and has shadowed no hunt. Korvash left a message at the cairn base. Gorrak will tell more at the Goat's Throat in the dark of the moon (about nine days).

Day 3-10: Veshra never had word from Tessa. Hobb Teyl says Dargan taught his children the Weeping Ledge shelter above the Throat. Town gossip (Persuasion 17): a salt-peddler named Marl Quill says a hooded girl twice left a bundle of goat-cheeses at the Seven Crooks inn's back step, paid in carved horn tokens, always at dusk, last seen four days before Day 3 heading up the high road.

Day 10: Korvash left word at the Seven Crooks (innkeeper and Marl Quill) for the hooded girl: 'Korvash lives. Veshra's door is open.' Day 11: at the cairn found a reply scratched beneath his own: 'Not yet.' with Tessa's crescent mark; the goat figure gone. Someone with Tessa's mark is alive and nearby, or was within days.

Day 11 dawn: after Korvash called into the dark in Draconic, nothing answered but he found at first light the horn goat on a flat stone on the east path, with a slate chip scratched in Draconic: 'Greyshaft. Third gate. Don't let him see you know me.' The writer is almost certainly Tessa or someone who knows her marks; the identity of 'him' is probably the Foreman or Gorrak. She will be at Greyshaft's third gate.

Day 11 morning: Korvash vowed not to show he knows her and tells no one, not even Gorrak. Heads for Greyshaft to arrive 'loud and sullen and bound by oath.' Third gate of Greyshaft is the meeting place. Midwinter's eve is the deadline.

Day 15 dusk: at the second gallery door, Korvash hears the hooded mender at the third-gate wash-line singing the clan's goat-counting song, the one Dargan sang; she hit the verse about the 'seventh goat that returns' twice, pointedly. The Foreman's guards did not notice. She has not looked down.

Day 16 dusk: Korvash hummed the answering lines; Pip wrote it down but accepted the sentiment. The mender answered with the wash-line: cloths hung grey, red, grey, an old clan field signal meaning 'meet by water after dark'. The third-gate wash-house sluice runs down to a stone culvert opening at the foot of the second wall, east side, behind the coal sheds; it is unguarded after the dusk bell except for a drunk pair on the wall above. Meeting set for after the second night bell.

DONE Day 16: Tessa found alive at Greyshaft's culvert. New purpose: help her break the Foreman's ledger and free the children in the lower galleries before midwinter's eve (Day 20), when the ledger and a hundred 'hands' move to the deep shaft.

Old goat-keeper in Harrowmere, once of Korvash's clan; knew the secret goat-paths and rock shelters around the Goat's Throat (including the Weeping Ledge, a cave behind a seep). Says Dargan taught the paths to both his children.
Hidden shelter in the rocks above the Goat's Throat behind a water seep; only clan members of Dargan's household knew it. Possible hiding place of the hooded figure.

Deadline for Korvash to report to Greyshaft's gate. DM ruling: it falls on Day 20, nine days after Day 11 (Day 11 = 5:58 AM when Korvash left the cairn). Greyshaft is three days' road from the Goat's Throat.

Pair of hobgoblin riders-on-foot in grey cloaks, sent by the Greyshaft Foreman to watch the road north of the Throat. Day 12 afternoon: Korvash spotted them on a ridge, shadowing him from half a mile off. They have not closed.

Day 12 night: Korvash's sullen act (Deception natural 1) overplayed: too loud, too much; the scouts doubt it. One of them ran ahead to Greyshaft to report he 'acts like a man with something to hide'; the other shadows him until the gate. The Foreman will have him watched.

Young goblin ledger-boy at Greyshaft, the Foreman's watcher assigned as Korvash's bunkmate; quick, bright-eyed, chatters; reports nightly to the Counting House. Can be bribed with rations or befriended.

Day 14 afternoon: befriended by Korvash with goat meat (Persuasion 13). Told him: shifts change at dawn, noon and dusk bells; water carts come at the noon bell; the guards of the second wall drink on watch after the dusk bell; the third gate is the Foreman's ledger-house and its stairs, guarded by six Tally-sworn hobgoblins, never drunk. A quiet girl, a mender 'who mends the ledger-bindings and sings to goats that aren't there', came with the autumn tally and sleeps in the ledger-house; Pip has only seen her at the gate-top wash-line at dusk. She wears a hood.
Day 21 ~5 PM: after the Foreman's death, Pip appeared at the ledger-house, shaken, asking where a ledger-boy goes when the ledger's gone; asked to come along to Harrowmere.
Day 21 evening: Korvash invited Pip to come to Harrowmere and keep Aunt Veshra's flour accounts, with a bunk at her table. Pip shared Korvash's bread.

Drunk hobgoblin guard of Greyshaft's second wall, east side. Day 16 night: spotted Korvash slipping toward the coal sheds and challenged him from the stair; half-drunk, loud, curious, loyal to the Foreman's coin more than the Foreman.

Day 16 night: accepted Korvash's insomnia excuse and a strip of goat meat (Deception 11, just). Told him: 'Don't let the Foreman's boys see you east of the sheds after the bell, Emberhide. I never saw you.' Returned to the wall to drink with his mate. Owes Korvash nothing but will not volunteer the sighting unless asked.

Korvash's younger sister, alive. Day 16 night, ~10:30 PM, met him at the Greyshaft culvert. Small and wiry for a dragonborn, red scales dulled to rust, left horn broken, burn scar on one forearm; hooded; speaks Draconic in short clipped sentences; she cut her crescent mark. Survived the raid by hiding on the Weeping Ledge as a child; Dargan's cairn-stones hid her; Gorrak let her go. Lived in the rocks and as a goat-girl on far farms; took the mender's post at Greyshaft on purpose, one autumn ago, to learn the ledger. Wants to free the children held in the lower galleries and destroy the Foreman's ledger of 'hands'.

Clan cloth signals (Dargan's fold): grey alone = fair weather, nothing to report, hold the plan; grey-red-grey = meet at the stream after dark, come alone; red alone (single) = go now / the way is open. Day 18 dusk: three greys at the gate-top, then a single red cloth hung after Korvash tied his red thread.

Day 19 ~7:15 AM: Asked whether Gorrak Vael will be ally or the Foreman's, she said honestly she does not know: he let her go the night of the raid, but he fears the Foreman and the ledger counts him too. Day 19 ~8:10 AM: column reached the stream at the foot of the east track; Korvash chose to halt and wait for Vael there.

Day 20 ~4 AM: Korvash scuffed a message in Draconic under her crescent on the ore road ('Dusk. Lower gate. Ledger moves. Gorrak's number burns with it.') unseen by the Tallies. Column reaches Greyshaft's lower gate ~6 PM Day 20 after a day-long march with short halts.

Day 20 ~7:30 PM: Korvash hummed the goat-counting song in the deep shaft, unnoticed by guards. A faint answering three taps came from the rock behind the far wall of the gallery, in the rhythm of the counting song. A child said Gorrak was dragged up the third-gate stair by two grey cloaks; no one saw a hooded girl taken.

Day 20 ~7:40 PM: she answered Korvash's tapping from a seam in the deep shaft's far wall, opening it a crack to reach the shackle locks; her first pick attempt scraped loudly (7 vs 15). A guard with a singed beard picked up a torch and walked the row to look.
Day 20 ~7:41 PM: Korvash's feigned fever failed (nat 1, too theatrical); the singed-beard guard stopped just out of chain reach and spotted the lock-pick and a hooded shape against the wall.

Day 20 ~7:41 PM: dropped to 0 HP fighting the chest guards in the deep shaft (a child pile-on tripped a guard; she stabilized Korvash with Medicine 14). The guard knocked her out, stable; captured. ~9:45 PM: lies bound beside Korvash in the Foreman's bedchamber.

With Tessa, destroy the Greyshaft Foreman's ledger of 'hands' and free the children held in the lower galleries before Day 20 (midwinter's eve), when the ledger and about a hundred laborers are moved to the deep shaft. Complications: Korvash's year-and-a-day oath to the Iron Tallies; Gorrak Vael's debt and fear; Tally-Pip watches Korvash; third gate guarded by six Tally-sworn hobgoblins.

Day 16 night, Tessa's intel: the ledger-house crowns the third gate; six Tally-sworn hobgoblins hold the stair in two shifts of three (changing at the dusk bell and the dawn bell); a wash-house door on the gate-top roof is unlocked from inside by Tessa and opens onto the Foreman's outer room. The ledger sleeps in an iron-bound chest in the Foreman's bedchamber; the key is on a chain at his belt and he sleeps lightly. A second ledger, the copy, is in the Counting House by the lower gate. Plan window: the nights of Day 18 or 19, before the move on Day 20. Tessa can open the wash-house door any night at the second bell; Korvash can reach the gate-top roof via the sluice path and the wash-house drain-stair.

Plan agreed Day 16 night: night of Day 18: Korvash burns the copy in the Counting House first (he'll pull it from the shelf), then climbs the drain-stair to the third gate and Tessa lets him in at the second bell to burn the master ledger. Children are held in the Tin Row, a barred bunkhouse built into the cliff beneath the first gate (two hundred feet below the Counting House), 94 children, kept by Warden Hask and four wall-guards; its door key is on the Foreman's chain, but the Tin Row also has an old ore-chute at its back that Tessa has found, leading out to the scree on the east side. Signal: Korvash hangs a red thread on his belt at dusk on Day 18 if the way is clear. Tessa lamp-oil stash under the wash-house. Pip must be kept fed and bored.

Day 18 night: Korvash set fire to the east coal shed but his Stealth failed (6) and a Counting House door guard saw him; the alarm is rising. Night scribe still inside with the copy. Guard 2 ran to the fire; the second bell has not yet rung.

Day 18 ~6:08 PM: Korvash set the Counting House copy and shelves alight with the lamp oil; copy burning. The master ledger in the third-gate ledger-house remains. Korvash is at 2 HP in a burning room, the doorway held by Guard 1; second wall's torches closing.

Day 18 ~8:10 PM: Korvash fell at 0 HP in the burning Counting House; the Foreman's guards stabilized him (the Foreman wants him alive as a 'hand') and put the fire out, saving the shelves but not the copy ledger, which is ash. He is held in the Tin Row with the children, stripped of axe, handaxes, javelins, pouch (coins, Tessa's horn goat and slate chip), all taken to the Foreman. The Foreman may now know of a link to the mender (Tessa). Tessa will hear the alarm. Master ledger intact in the ledger-house. Midwinter's eve move is in two days.

Day 19 ~6:25 AM: Korvash tore out the Tin Row ore-chute grate frame (nat 20) and found behind it an old side-drift with rusted rails and a ladder rising toward the third gate, smelling of lamp oil and paper; Tessa's crescent is scratched on a rivet where she sawed it over nights. Tin Row door locked and wedged with a stool leg; Sentry A and B outside.

Day 19 ~6:30 AM: Korvash got out through the chute with the last children to the east scree to Tessa; sentries A and B raised the alarm; all 94 children free of the Row but pursuit expected. Master ledger still in the ledger-house; Korvash has 2 HP, no lamp oil, longsword and shield only.

Day 19 ~6:50 AM: Tessa leads 94 children down the east goat-track gully with Ninna counting; Korvash's slate-pull failed (12) and only half the slope came down; two of the Foreman's grey-cloaked scouts have caught up on the ridge above the gully.

Day 19 ~7:10 AM: Korvash's nat-20 Intimidation unnerved the two scouts; they backed off and one let slip the Foreman ordered them to follow and count, not fight, and that a rider already went to Gorrak Vael at Cinder Ford: Vael will be on the road by dusk. Scouts shadow the column from afar.

Day 20 ~6:10 PM (midwinter's eve): at the lower-gate yard, Korvash grappled the Foreman and tore off the key chain; Gorrak cut his chain and sided with him but the six Stair Guards obeyed the Foreman. Korvash dropped to 0, rose on a nat-20 death save, breathed fire (Foreman now 2 HP, two guards at 6 HP, litter scorched but ledger chest intact), then was knocked out (stable) by Guard 2. Gorrak lies knocked out and bleeding. The Foreman retook the keys and fled up the stair. Day 20 ~7:10 PM: Korvash wakes shackled in the deep shaft with the Tin Row's remnants; the chest was carried down too. Tessa's red cloth was the 'go' signal; her whereabouts unknown.

Day 21 ~2 PM: the Foreman is dead; the scorched master ledger sits on his desk in the ledger-house, under Gorrak's and Dreg's eyes; Tessa has the key chain. Korvash has not yet burned it; decision pending (Gorrak's debt is in it, along with the Tallies' tallies). Oath to the Tallies still stands unless Gorrak releases it.

Day 21 ~2 PM: Korvash burned the master ledger page by page in the ledger-house stove before the Tallies in the doorway. Quest accomplished. Gorrak accepted freeing all captives in Greyshaft and a meal at Veshra's, but refused (Persuasion nat 1) that Tally-sworn may leave freely at will; Tally-sworn answer to him.
Hobgoblin warden of the Tin Row, the barred bunkhouse where Greyshaft's captive children sleep; keeps four wall-guards. Methodical, joyless, drinks nothing. Carries a ring of keys.

Day 18 night: took custody of Korvash in the Tin Row on the Foreman's orders; chained him by one ankle to a ring at the end of the row beside the children. Methodical, took his belt and pouch to the Foreman.

Day 19 ~5:55 AM: choked unconscious by Korvash, bound and gagged with blanket strips. Four wall-guards of the Tin Row were bound asleep with rope. Korvash holds the key ring. The Tin Row is unlocked but still unnoticed from outside (dawn bell has just rung).

About ten years old, in the Tin Row at Greyshaft; unsurprised, shrewd, a herders' daughter from the lower steadings. Told Korvash (Day 18 night): the ore-chute at the back is a cellar-hatch fifteen paces behind the last bunk, a square iron grate bolted from the outside, wide enough for ten-year-olds; the older ones won't fit. A hooded mender came two nights ago with bread and told the children to 'wait until a goat sings.' Hask keeps all keys on the ring in his lap, including the one for Korvash's manacle; he counts the children each dawn and dusk and sleeps at his stool in shifts with four wall-guards at the door.

Day 19 pre-dawn: agreed with Korvash to have the smallest children loosen the chute-grate nuts at dawn if they can, to cough and moan about the 'dying' man at the dawn count, and to wait for the mender's goat-song. Korvash rested the night (long rest, undisturbed).

Day 19 ~6:20 AM: organized the children in tens at the chute, littlest first, older carrying the little ones. About thirty were out onto the east scree when a wall sentry noticed. Tessa's goat-song is heard from outside.

Tally-sworn guard of the Greyshaft ledger-house, the one with the singed beard (Korvash burned it Day 20). Turned against the Foreman when Gorrak read his debt line aloud; fought Guard 3 and was struck down. Held in the deep shaft with Korvash and Gorrak.
Day 21 ~2:35 AM: gave his name to Korvash; twelve years in Greyshaft, knows the stair guards' shifts. Wounded: split head, swollen arm.
Tally-sworn stair guard (the fifth guard, who dropped his sword when Gorrak read the ledger line). Young, frightened of the Foreman, but one of the four who asked Gorrak his number.

Day 21 ~2:40 AM: was the farther of the two spearmen at the deep-shaft door; flinched at his name but said nothing. The nearer spearman (a grey-cloak) overheard Korvash's whisper about Dreg and the dawn bell and reported it up the stair.
Day 21 morning: sided with Dreg and Gorrak's Tallies in storming the stair.

Day 22 evening at Hollin Cairn Camp: asked whether the Tally-sworn would be let into Harrowmere. Korvash promised they'd wait at the Border Stones, helms off and spears sheathed, under his eye until he speaks for them; he will bring the story of the stair door to Aunt Veshra and the drover Hale Orrin.
Sheltered hollow with a spring beside the ore road, a day's slow walk below Greyshaft. The freed column camped here on Day 22 night. Harrowmere is about another day's walk beyond.
